title: Consolidation: overlap receipt for the open selected-replay tooling PRs; #1142 fails on main and collides with #1108 (no new kappa)
body:
**Consolidation receipt. No new κ, no disposition, nothing closed.** The selected frontier, pinned files and `upstream/` are unchanged.

This adds one package, `research/selected-replay-tooling-receipt/`, with three parts:
- `RECEIPT.json`: exact-head overlap and retention facts for eight open PRs;
- `verify.py`: a stdlib checker;
- a README.

**Family.** Seven of the PRs have the selected #1094 cold replay path (1094 → 1042 → 799 → 741) as their premise: #1101, #1142, #1151, #1277, #1361, #1509 and #1646. The eighth, #1108, is included because #1142 re-adds its package. Four of them (#1101, #1108, #1142, #1151) are in `QUEUE-CURSOR.json`'s next batch.

## Findings, at base `1f7a9349`

- **Nothing in this family is already on main.** No changed path has an identical blob at the base. All eight heads apply cleanly.
- **#1142 (`0c2873e6`) fails on current main.**
  - Its capsule audit pins `certificates/selected-result.json` to the #1042 record (sha256 `207d1f49…`). That path now holds #1094's record.
  - The #1042 record is retained byte for byte at `certificates/checkpoints/frontier1042.json`. Changing only that one path in `PINS.json` makes it pass; I tested this in scratch and did not include it here.
  - Its documented `make frontier1042-capsule-closure-verify` target does not exist.
- **#1142 bundles an earlier copy of #1108's package** `research/compact-boundary-cancellation-seed51/`.
  - 5 of the 7 files still differ after CRLF normalization. #1142's copy pins the #942 blob at `selected-result.json` and fails with `Source drift`; #1108's copy passes.
  - Merging either PR and then the other gives an add/add conflict.
- **The other six heads' own checks pass at the trial merge with main:**
  - #1101: 8 tests;
  - #1108;
  - #1151: `verify.py`, 155 s on a loaded host;
  - #1277;
  - #1361: 35 live pins, 0 drift, 21 tests;
  - #1509.

  #1646 is based on main and was not rerun.
- **#1277's premise still holds:** `verify_frontier1094.py:82` discards `check_selected`'s result.
- **No overlap between members.** Apart from the #1108/#1142 collision, no two PRs change the same file. The pairs that look alike cover different steps:
  - #1151 and #1646 cover the lec and phases steps of the frontier1042 chain;
  - #1101 and #1509 cover bit589 scheduling and Boost;
  - #1277, #1361 and #1142 cover the reuse binding, CI drift and the archive bytes.

  The speed-ups (#1101, #1151, #1646) are opt-in and unwired. Their equality evidence differs: #1151 has byte-identical receipts, #1646 the pinned digests, and #1101 matches only after masking timing fields.

## Checks

- `python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/selected-replay-tooling-receipt --check-only`: `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS`.
- `python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/selected-replay-tooling-receipt`: `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`. The default `verify.py` checks the base-side facts and that five mutated receipts are rejected. It also passes on 3.10 and 3.14.
- `verify.py --heads`, after fetching `pull/N/head` for the eight PRs, recomputes these per-PR facts:
  - changed paths;
  - retention;
  - clean application;
  - the #1108/#1142 bytes, pin and conflict;
  - #1142's capsule pin.

  It passes on 3.14.
- `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py'`: 20 OK, 1 skipped. `git diff --check` is clean.
- **Not checked:** any PR's mathematics or speed claims beyond its own verifier, the cold `make frontier1094-verify`, Linux, and PRs outside the family.

## Task and overlap

- Card `overlap-receipt` (consolidation), chooser nonce `79f6b98a8835aa3644ac7e560756166d`, priority revision 3.
- Scope **refined** to this named family; the reason is in TASK.json. The other card, `scope-navigation`, was dropped because #1232 and #1285 already cover its obvious targets.
- `find_overlap.py --refresh` (05:17Z, 595 open PRs and 296 discussions, complete pagination) found no family receipt. It is not a novelty proof.
- Claim and finding: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18915531

## Open next questions

1. Repin #1142 and drop its seed51 copy? This needs the contributor or a maintainer.
2. Next-batch path collisions. I ran an unregistered scan of the 100 `next_batch` heads; details are in the README. Besides #1108/#1142, these conflict textually:
   - #1110/#1190 (`pr-ledger.md`);
   - #1112/#1137 (`Makefile`);
   - `.gitattributes` across the gauge44-ends7 family and #1193;
   - #1172 against #1107/#1117/#1121/#1124/#1130 inside `research/gauge44-ends7-t16/`. These look like competing package versions.
3. Whether to wire the opt-in speedups into the pinned cold chain. This needs a maintainer.

## Credit

- The PR authors: rcfc-jreed, martinxxx9, thakrarsagar, and JosieElliston for #1646.
- Douglas Colkitt: the efficient-review queue cursor and the selected replay archives.

**AI disclosure.** Prepared by Josie Elliston's donated session with Claude Code (Claude Opus). A Codex read-only review raised four points, all fixed. The equality claims of the speed-up PRs are now stated separately. `--heads` now checks pairwise path disjointness, with a control. The cold-chain and #1277 checks are tighter. The wording on #1646's base is corrected. There was no independent human review. Apache-2.0.
